title: Getting to and around Uttarakhand
sub: Airports, trains, buses, taxis and mountain-road planning
intro: Most trips start at one of four hubs: Delhi (the usual origin), Dehradun and Haridwar for Garhwal, and Kathgodam for Kumaon. Times below are typical and vary with traffic, weather and road work; they are not live information.

list: Jolly Grant Airport (Dehradun) is the main airport for Garhwal, Rishikesh, Haridwar and the Char Dham.
Pantnagar Airport serves Kumaon (Nainital, Corbett) with a limited schedule.
Some small airstrips (such as Naini Saini near Pithoragarh) have irregular service. Confirm before planning around them.
Haridwar and Dehradun are the main railheads for Garhwal; Yog Nagari Rishikesh has limited services.
Kathgodam is the main railhead for Nainital, Almora, Ranikhet and Kausani.
Kotdwar serves Lansdowne; Ramnagar serves Corbett; Tanakpur serves the far east.
There is no railway in the high hills. Connections to the mountains are by road only.
Delhi to Haridwar: about 4-5 hours.
Delhi to Dehradun: about 5-6 hours.
Delhi to Rishikesh: about 5-6 hours.
Delhi to Kathgodam or Nainital: about 6-7 hours.
Delhi to Corbett (Ramnagar): about 5-6 hours.
State buses (UTC) and private operators connect main towns; booking in advance helps in peak season.
Shared jeeps and taxis run on many hill routes and often leave when full.
In remote areas, services can be one a day or less. Ask locally the day before.
A taxi with a driver used to mountain roads is the usual choice for multi-day trips.
Self-drive suits experienced drivers; mountain roads are narrow with blind bends.
Motorcycle trips are popular but take extra care on wet and loose roads.
Avoid driving at night.
In monsoon (July-September), landslides can close roads for hours or days.
In winter, snow and ice can close roads above about 2,000 m.
Check road status with local police, district administration or the state disaster management channels before long journeys.
Keep a buffer day in your plan.

sections.p: Many places end at a road head: Kedarnath at Sonprayag/Gaurikund, Yamunotri at Janki Chatti, Valley of Flowers at Govindghat. From there you walk or take a pony, palki or porter. Fares are usually regulated locally. Ask at official counters rather than agreeing a price on the road.

Most hill sites involve stairs, steep roads and uneven paths. Elderly travellers and people with mobility needs should favour road-accessible destinations such as Mussoorie, Nainital, Haridwar, Badrinath and Gangotri, and check accessibility before booking.

faq.q: What is the best way to get around?
faq.a: A hired car with an experienced driver gives the most flexibility. Public transport works for main routes but is slow and infrequent on side roads.

title: First-time visitor's guide to Uttarakhand
sub: Planning, budget, packing, health and common mistakes
intro: Uttarakhand is a mountain state: distances look short on a map but take long on the road. This guide helps you plan realistically.

list: Pick a month first: it decides which places are open and safe (see the best-time guide).
Choose one region (Garhwal or Kumaon) for a short trip; do not try to cover both in a week.
Limit driving to about 5-6 hours on mountain days.
Add one buffer day to any trip of five days or more.
Book accommodation first in peak months (May-June, October-November).
1 day: Rishikesh, Haridwar, Mussoorie or Nainital.
2-3 days: Mussoorie and Dhanaulti, Nainital and lakes, Rishikesh and Haridwar.
4-6 days: Kumaon circuit, Auli, Chopta.
7+ days: Garhwal or Kumaon loops, Char Dham, a trek.

sections.p: Use the budget estimator on the Plan page with your own quoted prices. The main costs are vehicle hire, accommodation, meals and activities. Prices vary widely by season and place; get quotes and check them on official or booking sites.

list: Layers: base, mid and a windproof outer layer
Rain jacket or poncho
Comfortable walking shoes with grip
Warm cap and gloves if above 2,000 m
Sun protection
Personal medication and a small first-aid kit
Power bank and offline maps
ID and copies of bookings

sections.p: Altitude sickness can affect anyone above about 2,500 m. Ascend gradually, drink water, and rest. Descend if symptoms worsen. Consult a doctor first if you have heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions.

list: ATMs are common in towns but scarce in remote areas; carry cash.
Mobile coverage is patchy in valleys and above villages; download offline maps.
Emergency numbers: 112 (national emergency), 108 (ambulance). Confirm the current local helplines on official sites.
Consider travel insurance, especially for treks and monsoon travel.
Choose road-accessible destinations.
Shorter driving days and slower itineraries.
Check medical facilities along the route.
Packing too many stops into too few days.
Driving at night.
Ignoring weather and landslide alerts.
Assuming ATMs, fuel and network are available everywhere.
Not booking in peak season.
Uttarakhand Tourism Development Board
India Meteorological Department (weather and rainfall alerts)
District administration pages for road and permit information

faq.q: How many days do I need for Uttarakhand?
faq.a: For one region, 5-7 days is comfortable. A single city or town can be done in 1-2.

title: Trek preparation and packing guide
sub: What to carry for day hikes, supported treks and self-supported trips
intro: Preparation matters more than fitness alone. Use this list as a starting point and follow your operator's advice. Do not trek high altitude alone or unsupported if you are not experienced.

list: Small daypack with rain cover
Sturdy shoes with grip and good socks
Water bottle (1-2 L) and snacks
Rain jacket and a warm layer
Sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat
Basic first-aid kit and personal medication
ID, phone, power bank and offline maps
Backpack (40-60 L) with rain cover
Trekking shoes broken-in before the trip, plus spare socks
Layered clothing: base, fleece, insulated jacket, thermal wear if cold
Waterproof jacket and pants
Water bottles (2-3 L), and purification tablets or filter
Energy snacks
Headlamp with spare batteries
Trekking poles (helps knees on descents)
Sleeping bag and tent are usually supplied by operators; confirm
First-aid kit and personal medicines
ID, permits, emergency contacts

sections.p: Do not attempt unsupported high-altitude routes unless you have experience, proper permits, communication and rescue arrangements. For routes like Auden's Col, use a registered expedition operator.

list: Ascend slowly; limit gain in sleeping altitude per day.
Drink water, eat well, avoid alcohol.
Headache, nausea or breathlessness that worsens means descend.
Tell your guide about any medical condition.
Carry out all litter.
Do not camp outside designated sites.
Respect local people, sacred sites and wildlife.
Use biodegradable soap away from water sources.

faq.a: For snow, high passes and remote routes, yes. For short easy day hikes in summer a guide is optional.

title: Where to stay in Uttarakhand
sub: Hotels, homestays, camps, ashrams and government accommodation
intro: This guide explains the types of stay. It does not list specific properties, prices or ratings. For current availability use the official or reputable booking sites linked below.

sections.p: Available in nearly every tourist town. Look for properties with parking and clear road access, and read recent reviews on a reputable booking site.
Good for villages and treks. They offer home-cooked food and local advice. Confirm last-mile road access, heating and Wi-Fi with the host.
Use camps run by licensed operators with clear safety standards. Avoid sleeping in unofficial sites or near riverbeds.
Common in Haridwar, Rishikesh and along pilgrim routes. They are simple, often have rules about timings, and may require advance booking.
GMVN (Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam) and KMVN (Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam) run rest houses in many places. Forest rest houses are available for eligible visitors through the forest department.

list: Mussoorie: near Library or Landour for quiet.
Nainital: Tallital or Mallital depending on walking.
Rishikesh: Tapovan for cafes, further out for quiet.
Char Dham: choose the base town for the road head, not the temple itself in peak season.

links.label: GMVN (Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam; address as listed in its rest-house details)

faq.a: For May-June, Char Dham and festival dates, book well ahead. Off-season is easier.

title: Culture, food and festivals
sub: Garhwali and Kumaoni traditions, local dishes and fairs
intro: Uttarakhand's two regions, Garhwal and Kumaon, share many traditions but have their own dialects, dishes and festivals.

sections.p: Garhwal is in the west (Dehradun, Rishikesh, Char Dham). Kumaon is in the east (Nainital, Almora). Each has its own folk songs, dances and festival calendar.

list: Aloo ke Gutke: spiced potatoes
Kafuli: spinach and fenugreek gravy
Bhatt ki Churkani: black soybean curry
Mandua ki Roti: finger millet flatbread
Garhwali Kadhi and Phaanu: lentil and yogurt dishes
Jhangora ki Kheer: barnyard millet pudding
Singori and Bal Mithai (Kumaon): sweets from Almora
Arsa: sweet rice-flour fried cookies
Makar Sankranti / Uttarayani (January): fairs such as at Bageshwar.
Holi (March): Kumaoni Baithaki Holi is a local tradition.
Harela (July): a Kumaon festival marking sowing.
Nanda Devi fairs (September): in Almora, Nainital and other places.
Dussehra and Diwali (October-November).
Kumbh Mela at Haridwar every 12 years; the Ardh Kumbh is reported to run from 14 January to 20 April 2027, so expect heavy crowds.
Choliya (a sword dance), Jhora and Chancheri are well-known folk dances.
Aipan is a floor art form in Kumaon.
Woollens and handwoven shawls are sold in places like Munsiyari and Pithoragarh.
Remove shoes at temples; dress modestly.
Ask before photographing people or rituals.
Do not litter, and carry a bag for rubbish.
Many shrines restrict leather and non-vegetarian food.

faq.q: What local dish should I try first?
faq.a: Bhatt ki churkani or mandua roti with local ghee, and bal mithai for dessert.

title: Wildlife and national parks
sub: Corbett, Rajaji, Nanda Devi, Valley of Flowers and sanctuaries
intro: Uttarakhand has national parks, tiger reserves and sanctuaries. Rules on permits and safaris change often; use official sources.

sections.p: Tiger reserve in the Kumaon foothills. Per the official site (corbettgov.org): Jhirna, Dhela and Garjia are open all year; Bijrani is open 15 October to 30 June; Dhikala, Durgadevi, Sonanadi and Pakhro 15 November to 15 June. Book only on the official site (booking.corbettgov.org); it warns about scam booking sites. Valid ID must match the ID uploaded at booking, and mobile phones are not permitted in tourism zones.
Forest reserve near Haridwar and Rishikesh, known for elephants. Safaris run from a few gates.

sections.h: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
sections.p: A UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Valley of Flowers opened on 1 June 2026 and was reported open to 31 October; the core of Nanda Devi National Park is restricted.

High-altitude park; permits are needed for treks inside, including Gaumukh. Secondary 2026 guides report a daily cap of 150 and a mandatory guide, insurance and medical certificate; confirm with the Uttarkashi forest office.
Govind Pashu Vihar covers the Har Ki Dun and Kedarkantha area. Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary near Almora offers forest walks with an entry fee.

list: Keep a safe distance; never feed animals.
Stay in the vehicle on safari.
Do not expect a sighting; tigers are rarely seen.
Use only licensed guides and official booking channels.

faq.q: Can I book a Corbett safari on arrival?
faq.a: Usually not. Book online in advance through the official channel.

title: Peaceful, less-crowded places
sub: Quieter villages and hill stations. Relatively quiet, never guaranteed empty
intro: These places are generally quieter than Mussoorie or Nainital, especially on weekdays and in the off-season. Crowds vary by weekend, holiday and year, and we cannot guarantee any place will be quiet.

Stay: resorts, camps and homestays.

Why quiet: birdwatching villages close to Nainital.

Why quiet: far from main routes with long road journeys.

Stay in locally owned homestays.
